metaTitle: White Cockroach: Is It an Albino Roach? (Photos)
metaDescription: A white cockroach is a normal roach that just molted, not an albino, and it darkens within hours. Photos, what it means and white bugs mistaken for one.
h1: White Cockroach: What a White or Albino Roach Really Is
dek: Every cockroach turns white each time it sheds its skin, then darkens within hours. Real photos of white roaches, why true albinos are lab oddities, what seeing one says about roaches nearby, and the pale bugs that look like one.
excerpt: Why some cockroaches are white: molting, not albinism. Photos, how long a roach stays white, what one means in your house, and the white bugs mistaken for roaches.

quickAnswer.lead: **A white cockroach is an ordinary cockroach that has just shed its skin, not an albino or a separate species: it has a cockroach's flat body, a head hidden under a shield and long, thin antennae, and it darkens within hours as its new outer covering hardens.** [UC IPM's cockroach guide](https://ipm.ucanr.edu/home-and-landscape/cockroaches/) gives that timing; a white insect without those features is something else.
bullets: Every cockroach is white for a few hours after each molt; German nymphs molt 5 to 6 times before they become adults, according to [Rutgers University](https://njaes.rutgers.edu/fs1322/).

A white roach is its species' usual size: German nymphs measure 1/8 to 9/16 inch (Rutgers), and adult American cockroaches 1 1/2 to 2 inches ([Texas A&M AgriLife Extension](https://extensionentomology.tamu.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2017/12/Cockroach-Biol-and-Mngmt_ENTO-037_2017.pdf)).

True albinos are lab oddities: [NC State entomologist Coby Schal](https://schal-lab.cals.ncsu.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/402/2018/10/2011Schal_Mallis_Fact_or_Fiction.pdf) writes that albino mutants turn up occasionally in lab colonies and are extremely unlikely to be found outside the lab.

Newly hatched nymphs are often pale too: the [University of Florida](https://ask.ifas.ufl.edu/publication/IN298) says a first-stage American cockroach nymph is white right after hatching, then turns grayish brown.
Only nymphs molt, so a white roach means young roaches are growing up in or near the home; about 80 percent of an actively growing German cockroach population are nymphs (Rutgers).

body.text: What is a white cockroach?

A white cockroach is an ordinary cockroach that has just molted, or shed its skin. The [University of California's Pest Notes on cockroaches](https://ipm.ucanr.edu/home-and-landscape/cockroaches/) (UC IPM) say cockroaches are white immediately after molting and darken as the outer covering hardens, usually within hours. Walter Ebeling's *Urban Entomology*, a 1975 textbook hosted by [UC Riverside's entomology department](https://entomology.ucr.edu/ebelingchapter6), notes that completely white nymphs or adults may be seen in a cockroach colony, newly molted and not yet their species' normal color.

body.alt: Cream-white cockroach with dark eyes and small crumpled wings on a wooden board, beside a dark reddish-brown cast skin split open behind the head
body.caption: A freshly molted American cockroach, still white with its new wings crumpled, beside a dark shed skin split open at the thorax. The observer recorded it molting in a chicken coop in Georgia.

body.text: So it is not a separate kind of cockroach: a white German cockroach is a German cockroach, at the usual size for its stage. [Nebraska Extension's cockroach management manual](https://hles.unl.edu/sites/unl.edu.ianr.extension.community-environment/files/media/file/CockroachManual_2022.pdf) says homeowners occasionally come across a white cockroach and that it is not an albino. Its species shows once it darkens, and [the complete guide to cockroaches in US homes](/learn/cockroaches) profiles each one.

Check the shape first. [Texas A&M AgriLife Extension](https://extensionentomology.tamu.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2017/12/Cockroach-Biol-and-Mngmt_ENTO-037_2017.pdf) lists what every cockroach has: a flattened body, a head hidden from above under a plate-like shield called the pronotum, long, thin antennae and long, spiny legs. A white insect without them is probably one of the look-alikes further down.

body.needed: A freshly molted, still-white German cockroach nymph or adult beside a ruler marked in inches, identified to species by an entomologist or extension service; public domain or CC0 so it could lead the page

body.text: Are albino cockroaches real?

Yes, as rare laboratory mutants. In a question-and-answer article for pest professionals, excerpted from the *Mallis Handbook of Pest Control* and posted by his NC State lab, entomologist [Coby Schal](https://schal-lab.cals.ncsu.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/402/2018/10/2011Schal_Mallis_Fact_or_Fiction.pdf) writes that all newly molted cockroaches are white and that the wings and body tan to the species' color and pattern over the next several hours. Albino and white-eyed mutants, he adds, are occasionally found in lab colonies but are extremely unlikely to be found outside the lab. The white roach in a kitchen or basement is almost certainly a freshly molted one.
Why does a cockroach turn white when it molts?

Because its new outer skin starts out nearly colorless. To grow, an insect builds a larger skeleton inside the old one and then sheds the old one. [NC State University's general entomology course](https://genent.cals.ncsu.edu/bug-bytes/morphogenesis) explains that muscle contractions and air the insect takes in split the old skeleton along lines of weakness. The insect climbs out soft and largely unpigmented, white or ivory, and over the next few hours a process called sclerotization, or tanning, hardens and darkens the new skin.

body.alt: Cockroach halfway out of its old skin on a white surface, its pale cream head, legs and body pulling free of the reddish-brown skin still around its abdomen
body.caption: A cockroach halfway through a molt in a building's bathroom in Louisiana, its pale new body pulling free of the old reddish-brown skin. The species was not identified.
body.credit: abbeyprivate, Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons

body.text: Nymphs molt at the end of each growth stage, and molting stops once an insect is an adult, the course adds. [Rutgers University's German cockroach fact sheet](https://njaes.rutgers.edu/fs1322/) says German nymphs molt 5 to 6 times; other common species go through more stages:

head: Species
Nymph stages (each ends in a molt)
Adult length
body.caption: Nymph stages: Nebraska Extension, adapted from Brenner and Kramer (2019). Other sources differ: 5 to 6 molts for German nymphs (Rutgers), 6 to 14 for American (University of Florida). Lengths: Texas A&M and UC IPM.

body.text: How long does a cockroach stay white?

A few hours. UC IPM says usually within hours; the [University of Florida's German cockroach profile](https://ask.ifas.ufl.edu/publication/IN128) says a newly molted adult's cuticle will harden and darken within a few hours; Nebraska's manual says a couple of hours; and [Kansas State University's cockroach fact sheet](https://bookstore.ksre.ksu.edu/pubs/MF2765.pdf) says nymphs appear white for several hours.

The closest measurement in these sources is a 1940 laboratory study of American cockroaches by Gould and Deay, reported by Ebeling: molting took only a few minutes, and a new adult's wings needed 25 to 30 minutes to expand and its full color 4 or 5 hours. A white roach with small, crumpled wings, like the one in the first photo, has molted very recently.

body.alt: Cream-white adult cockroach with black eyes, long antennae and fully expanded pale wings, seen from above on a rough gray stucco wall
body.caption: A white adult American cockroach on a textured wall in Texas. The iNaturalist user who identified it noted that it was white because it had recently molted.
body.credit: (c) Meghan Cassidy, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), via iNaturalist

body.text: That gives you a simple check: trap the insect in a closed jar and look again a few hours later. A freshly molted cockroach should have darkened toward its species' colors, which also makes it easier to identify.
Why do you rarely see a white cockroach?

Because the white stage is short and cockroaches spend most of their lives out of sight. UC IPM says roaches hide by day in warm, dark, moist places and feed at night, and Texas A&M says the German cockroach spends about 75 percent of its life in cracks 1/32 to 3/16 inch wide.

Seeing one by day says more about numbers. Texas A&M says cockroaches seen during the day usually mean there are a lot of them, and [NC State Extension's German cockroach guide](https://content.ces.ncsu.edu/biology-behavior-of-the-german-cockroach) says German cockroaches occasionally appear by day when the population is too crowded. Ebeling adds that when roaches are abundant, a few may be seen in daylight, particularly when things in pantries, cabinets and closets are moved.
What does a white cockroach in your house mean?

It means a cockroach molted within the last few hours, and only a growing roach does that: nymphs molt, adults never molt again. A white nymph is a young roach between stages; a white adult has just made its final molt.

With German cockroaches, that points to a colony in the building. Nebraska's manual says they breed indoors year-round and that more are hiding than are ever seen, NC State says small nymphs tend to stay at their aggregation sites, and Rutgers says about 80 percent of an actively growing German population are nymphs. A small white German nymph most likely hides close to where it turned up.

A white American or Oriental cockroach is a different case. The [University of Florida's American cockroach profile](https://ask.ifas.ufl.edu/publication/IN298) says that species lives mainly in basements, sewers and drainage systems and is rarely found in houses, though infestations can occur after heavy rain; Texas A&M puts Oriental cockroaches in basements, crawl spaces and wet areas. [The palmetto bug guide](/blog/palmetto-bugs) covers the American cockroach, and [the Oriental cockroach guide](/blog/oriental-cockroaches) the dark, short-winged Oriental.

body.alt: Three American cockroaches on rough gray concrete: one at the top with a white new body emerging from its reddish-brown skin, two dark reddish-brown adults below it
body.caption: One American cockroach (top) in the middle of a molt, its white new body coming out of the reddish-brown nymph skin, beside two dark adults. NY State IPM Program at Cornell University photo.
body.credit: NY State IPM Program at Cornell University from New York, USA, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

body.text: Then look for the other signs: Ebeling lists dead cockroaches, cast skins, empty egg cases and droppings. [The guide to signs of cockroaches](/blog/signs-of-cockroaches) goes through each, and [what roach poop looks like](/blog/cockroach-droppings) covers the droppings. UC IPM calls sticky traps the best way to detect and monitor cockroaches: put them where floors meet walls near the spot and check them daily for several days.
Is a white baby cockroach newly hatched or newly molted?

It can be either: nymphs are often pale when they hatch and white again after every molt. The University of Florida says a first-stage American cockroach nymph is white right after hatching, then grayish brown, and that later nymphs are white after each molt before turning reddish brown. Kansas State says hatchlings are usually lighter in color than adults.

body.alt: About a dozen tiny pale cockroach nymphs with dark eyes on a sticky trap around a tan, ridged egg case, beside a brown adult German cockroach
body.caption: Newly hatched German cockroach nymphs, still pale, stuck on a sticky trap around an egg case, beside an adult. The observer saw them hatching.

body.text: Tiny pale nymphs bunched beside an egg case are a fresh hatch; one white nymph among darker ones has just molted. Newly hatched German nymphs are about 1/8 inch (3 mm) long, NC State says, and the University of Florida describes German nymphs as dark brown to black with dark bands. Each species' young are shown side by side in [what baby cockroaches look like](/blog/what-do-baby-cockroaches-look-like), and [the guide to cockroach eggs](/blog/cockroach-eggs) covers the cases they hatch from.
What happens to the skin a cockroach sheds?

Often a cockroach eats it. Ebeling reports German cockroach skins quickly eaten by the nymphs that shed them or by others nearby, and, in Gould and Deay's study, American cockroaches usually eating the cast skin after every molt but the last. A skin that is left looks like a hollow copy of the roach, split open where it climbed out.

body.alt: Empty, translucent amber-and-brown banded skin of a young cockroach, with the casings of its legs and antennae trailing from it, on brown cardboard
body.caption: The empty shed skin of a young cockroach in the genus Blattella, which includes the German cockroach, on cardboard in Texas.

body.text: Skins that remain are evidence: UC IPM lists cast skins among the signs that show where to place monitoring traps. Rutgers says German cockroach feces, shed skins and dead bodies contain allergens that are asthma triggers, and recommends a vacuum with a HEPA filter to remove them.

A pale, empty skin in a mattress seam is more likely a bed bug's. The [EPA's guide to finding bed bugs](https://www.epa.gov/bedbugs/how-find-bed-bugs) lists the pale yellow skins that nymphs shed as they grow among the signs, and [bed bug shells and shed skins](/blog/bed-bug-shells-casings-shed-skins-canada) shows what they look like.
What else looks like a white cockroach?
Three pale insects can pass for a white roach at a glance. Run the shape check first; for brown and black look-alikes, see [bugs that look like cockroaches](/blog/bugs-that-look-like-cockroaches).
Termite workers

[Texas A&M's urban entomology program](https://urbanentomology.tamu.edu/urban-pests/termites/native/) describes native subterranean termite workers as wingless, white to creamy white and 1/4 to 3/8 inch long. The [EPA](https://www.epa.gov/safepestcontrol/termites-how-identify-and-control-them) says termites rarely emerge from the soil, mud tubes or the wood and other food they tunnel through. A worker stays pale, where a white cockroach darkens within hours. Pale insects in damaged wood or a mud tube point to termites; [what termite damage looks like](/blog/termite-damage) shows the tubes.
Booklice

Booklice are smaller than even a newly hatched cockroach. The [University of Florida's guide to booklice and silverfish](https://ask.ifas.ufl.edu/publication/IG094) describes soft-bodied insects, translucent white to gray or light brown, usually under 1/16 inch long and mostly wingless indoors, often found among books or papers in warm, humid places.
Bed bug nymphs

Young bed bugs are translucent or whitish-yellow and, unfed, can be nearly invisible, says the [EPA's bed bug life cycle page](https://www.epa.gov/bedbugs/bed-bugs-appearance-and-life-cycle), which gives the five nymph stages as 1.5 to 4.5 mm (about 1/16 to 3/16 inch). EPA says bed bugs hide near the seams and tags of mattresses and in cracks of the bed frame and headboard; [what bed bugs look like](/blog/what-do-bed-bugs-look-like) covers every stage.

body.text: What should you do about a white cockroach?
Treat it as a sign of cockroaches growing nearby, and work through these steps:

items: **Let it darken.** Keep it in a closed jar for a few hours, or photograph it now and later, then compare it with the species in [the complete cockroach guide](/learn/cockroaches).
**Set sticky traps** where floors meet walls near the spot and check them daily for several days, as UC IPM advises.
**Check for other signs** in nearby cracks, cabinets and appliances: droppings, egg cases and shed skins.

**Treat the species you have.** [The step-by-step plan for getting rid of cockroaches](/blog/how-to-get-rid-of-cockroaches) puts baits, traps and sealing in order, with [a Canadian edition](/blog/how-to-get-rid-of-cockroaches-canada) for readers in Canada; [the German cockroach guide](/blog/german-cockroaches) goes further for that species.

body.title: Save the evidence
body.text: Photograph the white insect beside a ruler marked in inches, then again a few hours later, and note where you found it. Your state's cooperative extension office or a pest professional can use those details to help identify it.

faqs.question: Is it normal to see a white cockroach?
faqs.answer: It is a normal stage but an unusual sight. Every cockroach is white for a few hours after each molt, and Rutgers University says German cockroach nymphs molt 5 to 6 times before adulthood. Most of that happens out of view, because cockroaches hide by day in cracks and dark places and come out at night to feed, UC IPM says. Seeing a white one tells you a roach molted recently, so young cockroaches are developing in or near your home.

faqs.question: How rare is an albino roach?
faqs.answer: A true albino cockroach is a laboratory rarity. Entomologist Coby Schal of NC State University writes that albino and white-eyed mutants are occasionally found in lab colonies but are extremely unlikely to be found outside the lab. The white roaches people find at home are freshly molted cockroaches: Schal notes that all newly molted cockroaches are white and tan to their normal color and pattern over the next several hours. Nebraska Extension's cockroach manual makes the same point.

faqs.question: What does it mean if I find a white cockroach in my house?
faqs.answer: It means a cockroach shed its skin within the last few hours, and only growing roaches do that, since adult insects stop molting. Nebraska Extension says German cockroaches breed indoors year-round, and Rutgers says about 80 percent of an actively growing German population are nymphs, so a white German cockroach points to a colony in the building. Set sticky traps where floors meet walls near the spot and check them daily for several days to see how many there are and where.

faqs.question: How long does a cockroach stay white?
faqs.answer: Usually a few hours. UC IPM says the outer covering darkens as it hardens, usually within hours, and the University of Florida says the same of a newly molted adult German cockroach. In a laboratory study of American cockroaches reported in Walter Ebeling's Urban Entomology, molting took only a few minutes, and a new adult's wings took 25 to 30 minutes to expand and its full color 4 or 5 hours. A white cockroach kept in a closed jar should have darkened within a few hours.

faqs.question: Is a white cockroach harmful?
faqs.answer: It is no different from any other cockroach of its species, just freshly molted. The concern is the infestation behind it. Rutgers says German cockroach feces, shed skins and dead bodies contain allergens that are asthma triggers, and NC State lists saliva, feces, eggs and shed exoskeletons as sources of cockroach allergens. Texas A&M adds that cockroaches may transfer disease-causing organisms. A white roach indoors is a reason to find and treat the colony it came from.

faqs.question: Can baby cockroaches be white?
faqs.answer: Yes, at two points in their lives. Nymphs are often pale when they first hatch: the University of Florida says a first-stage American cockroach nymph is white right after hatching and then turns grayish brown. They are white again after every molt until they become adults, darkening within hours each time. A cluster of tiny pale nymphs beside an egg case is a fresh hatch; newly hatched German cockroaches are about 1/8 inch long, according to NC State Extension.

faqs.question: What are the small white roaches in my house?
faqs.answer: Most likely young cockroaches that have just hatched or just molted, which darken within hours. Check the shape: Texas A&M says cockroaches have a flattened body, a head hidden under a shield, long thin antennae and spiny legs. Something under 1/16 inch among books or papers in a humid room is more likely a booklouse, a pale insect inside wood or a mud tube a termite worker, and a pale bug in a mattress seam a young bed bug.

faqs.question: Do cockroaches eat their shed skin?
faqs.answer: Often, yes. Walter Ebeling's Urban Entomology reports that German cockroach skins were quickly eaten by the nymphs that shed them or by other cockroaches nearby. In the laboratory study of American cockroaches he cites, the cast skin was usually eaten after every molt except the last, when the new adult left it behind. That is one reason shed skins are not always found, although UC IPM still lists cast skins among the signs of cockroach activity.

faqs.question: What should I do if I see a white roach?
faqs.answer: Identify it, then find out how many there are. Keep it in a closed jar or photograph it, and look again after a few hours, when it should have darkened enough to compare with photos of each species. Set sticky traps where floors meet walls nearby and check them daily for several days, as UC IPM advises. Look for droppings, egg cases and shed skins in nearby cracks and cabinets, then follow a control plan for the species you have.

faqs.question: Could a white cockroach be a termite?
faqs.answer: It could be a termite worker if the insect was inside wood, soil or a mud tube. Texas A&M describes native subterranean termite workers as wingless, white to creamy white and 1/4 to 3/8 inch long, and the EPA says termites rarely emerge from the soil, mud tubes or the wood and other food they tunnel through. A white cockroach has a shield over its head, long thin antennae and spiny legs, and it darkens within hours, while a worker stays pale.
